question: Should OpenClaw ship a signed standalone Android APK on GitHub Releases through the linked protected release workflow, and what signer/provenance policy must gate it?
rationale: A public sideload APK is a release-channel and signing-custody commitment; automation can verify source state but cannot choose the security/support boundary for official Android binaries.

options.title: Adopt the linked release workflow
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101212 if it satisfies signing custody, provenance, checksum, and stable-release gating.

options.title: Restrict Android distribution to Google Play for now
options.body: Keep this issue open or close it only after maintainers explicitly decide standalone GitHub Release APKs are unsupported.

options.title: Defer to another trusted channel
options.body: Keep the request open while designing F-Droid or another non-Play distribution path with equivalent provenance and support boundaries.

recommendation.title: Adopt the linked release workflow
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101212 if it satisfies signing custody, provenance, checksum, and stable-release gating.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to this issue and authored the active closing PR for the Android APK release workflow.
